title: Three and a half
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Thursday. Wood measures main street with his feet. It is three and a half blocks. The strip draws it that way: the panel is three and a half panels wide, and the fourth is cut.

panels.composition: Main street in rain. WOOD walking heel-to-toe, counting. BARNABY, one, behind him, not counting.

balloons.text: ...two hundred and eleven, two hundred and twelve —

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, a young man walking heel-to-toe down a rainy small-town street counting under his breath, a small dog behind him

panels.composition: The seawall end. Wood stopping. The count.

balloons.text: Three and a half. It was four in September.
(to the dog) You were here. You saw it.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, a young man stopped at a seawall in rain speaking to a small dog

panels.composition: The dog. Looking at the seawall. The seawall is where it always was.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, a small dog looking at a concrete seawall in rain, no words

panels.composition: The fourth panel: half width. The street, the two of them, cut off by the border mid-dog.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, a half-width panel of a rainy street with a young man and a small dog partly cut off by the panel's right border, no words
image.notes: Panel 4 is drawn at half width. The strip's narrowing device (dw_2000-10-02), now structural.

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: Three and a half blocks. The fourth panel half a panel.
